description: Machine-readable backend error identity. A code is a stable, language-independent identifier the frontend maps to presentation; the backend never ships display language beyond a developer-facing English message. Codes are `<namespace>.<reason>`, namespaces come from the domain registry (domains[].errorNamespace).
rules: A code is stable once published. Renaming or removing a code is a BREAKING change (see contract-lock.json).
A code's namespace must equal an errorNamespace declared in manifest/domains.json.
`status` is the HTTP status the compatibility layer emits for the code.
Message text is developer-facing English only. Localisation is the frontend's job (future Translation LEGO) and must key off `code`, never off the message string.
Adding a new code is a MINOR change; changing an existing code's `status` is BREAKING.

A code MAY declare `retryable` plus a `retryRationale`. Retryability is a property of the failure, not of the caller: it answers "could the identical call succeed later without anything else changing?". A caller must branch on this field rather than on the message string.

The `lego` namespace belongs to the lego-foundation domain and covers failures of the communication foundation itself (dispatch, negotiation, cancellation, backpressure) rather than of any feature domain.

statusSemantics.404: the addressed entity does not exist
statusSemantics.501: the capability is known but not implemented on this instance

codes.summary: Authenticated but the required scope is missing.
Login rejected.
Owner setup attempted on an instance that already has an owner.
No valid session for a protected route.
The addressed user does not exist.
Malformed request (body, query or params).
Unexpected server failure.
The request body exceeded the configured limit.
The addressed credential does not exist.
The credential type is not in the registry.
The run ended in an unhandled engine failure.
The addressed execution does not exist.
The run exceeded its time budget.
The consumer has no declared dependency on the capability it called.
codes.retryRationale: An architecture violation. Requires a manifest declaration, not a retry.

codes.summary: A stream consumer could not keep up and the declared policy is `reject`.
codes.retryRationale: Transient. The producer is ahead of the consumer, not broken.

codes.summary: A caller deliberately cancelled the operation.
codes.retryRationale: Deliberate. Retrying without a new decision would ignore the cancellation.

codes.summary: The capability exists in the registry but has no implementation here.
codes.retryRationale: Structural. Retrying cannot create an implementation.

codes.summary: The operation deadline passed before completion.
codes.retryRationale: Environmental. A retry with a fresh deadline may succeed.

codes.summary: A dependency is registered but its lifecycle state is not callable.
codes.retryRationale: Operational. The dependency may be re-enabled.

codes.summary: The caller used an interaction class the operation does not support.
codes.retryRationale: A caller bug. The same call will fail identically.

codes.summary: The capability needs a declared migration before it can be used.
codes.retryRationale: Requires the migration to be run.

codes.summary: The capability is available but does not implement this operation.
codes.retryRationale: Structural. The operation is absent from the contract.

codes.summary: The provider for a capability is not registered in this process.
codes.retryRationale: May become available once the owning LEGO is loaded.

codes.summary: The consumer requires a contract version the provider does not satisfy.
codes.retryRationale: Requires a migration or a version bump.

codes.summary: A declaration does not satisfy the contract it claims to implement — a missing required field, a malformed id, an unknown enum value or a duplicate registration.
codes.retryRationale: The declaration itself is wrong. The identical call will fail identically until the declaration is corrected.

codes.summary: The node catalog could not be read.
The addressed node type/version is not in the catalog.
Concurrent write conflict.
The addressed record does not exist.
The persistence backend could not be reached.
The capability is known but not implemented on this instance. `meta.feature`, `meta.owner` and `meta.phase` identify it. Kept namespace-free for backward compatibility with the P2 contract.
No workflow is listening on that webhook path.
The workflow changed since it was loaded.
The workflow payload failed validation.
The addressed workflow does not exist.
The addressed project does not exist.
